source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling (NVA8) publishes 24 MW of IT capacity across 154,230 square feet, placing it 17th among Virginia's 25 data centers that disclose power and holding 1.5 percent of the state's disclosed IT load.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 25 publish power capacity, totaling 1,603 MW. Most facilities disclose no figures, so the published ranking covers a small, self-selected slice of the state's actual compute footprint. Sterling's 24 MW is modest within that disclosed set, far below the largest sites.

For AI workloads, the operator publishes no certifications and no rack density, so whether the facility can host dense GPU clusters is not stated. At a common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 24 MW would support roughly 600 racks, but the operator does not confirm that density. The suitability score of 65 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing. Power supply, cooling, and grid interconnect details are absent, which limits any conclusion about its ability to support AI training at scale.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
